bugs.title: float/LongInt equality contradicts hashing: equal values, different hashes
bugs.description: eq_vals_depth compares float vs LongInt via num_as_f64 (lossy f64 rounding), so 1e16 == 10**16+1 is True (Python: False — it converts the float exactly). But hash_depth hashes the integral float as i64(1e16) and the LongInt as i64(10^16+1): different hashes for 'equal' values. Dict/get and ValSet operations disagree: d={1e16:'x'}; d.get(10**16+1) misses while 10**16+1 in {1e16} is True (contains uses a linear eq scan) and {1e16} & {10**16+1} is empty (ValSet uses hashes).
bugs.expected: Python: False / 'missing' / False — i.e. Python says not-equal so the miss is consistent; here eq says equal but the dict still misses, which is an internal invariant violation either way

bugs.title: Set -= rebinds instead of mutating in place
bugs.description: There is no InPlaceSub opcode; only InPlaceBitOr/And/Xor are handled (dispatch.rs:628). `s -= x` rebinds s to a new set, so aliases keep the old value. |=, &=, ^= mutate correctly.

bugs.title: MemoryError from a full heap is uncatchable
bugs.description: Entering an except handler allocates (the message string and the ExcInstance, via heap.alloc at dispatch.rs:236-241). When the heap is exhausted that allocation re-fails and the error propagates past the handler. A MemoryError raised by a pre-flight size check IS caught, confirming the mechanism.
bugs.actual: MemoryError: heap limit, exit code 1 (handler never runs)
bugs.notes: Also misformatted on the way out: the uncaught MemoryError prints bare to stdout instead of the normal 'error: ... --> file:line' stderr format other uncaught errors use.

bugs.title: User-defined __delitem__ corrupts subsequent method dispatch on the instance
bugs.description: After `del s[key]` runs a user __delitem__, any later method call or `in` check on the instance fails with AttributeError: 'object' object has no attribute '<attr>'. The deletion itself works. Plain del obj.attr and del list[i] are unaffected.

disorder.description: SerCtx.depth field was written once at construction and never read (actual depth is threaded through the separate `depth` parameter). Removed the field and its initializer; cargo check --manifest-path std/json/Cargo.toml passes.
Step comments are numbered 1. and 3. with no 2. (renumbering leftover; the unnumbered call_id comment at line 150 is the de-facto step 2). Comment-only fix left for the user.

Duplicated JSON string escapers: devkit.rs `escape` and snapshot.rs:708 `json_escape` implement the same escaping with slightly different \u handling. Not merged: devkit is std-only while snapshot is no_std, so removal is not trivially safe.
`.split('?').next().unwrap_or("/")` — str::split always yields at least one item, so the unwrap_or is dead (same pattern at engine/web.rs:232). Harmless; left in place.

Output format typo: PASS/FAIL lines use 'PASS - {description}' / 'FAIL - {description}' but the ERROR line is 'ERROR {description}' (missing ' - '). Baked into std/test/test.json expectations, so changing it needs a corpus update.
dict 'clear' is registered twice in ALL_METHODS (the appended group exists to keep snapshot method ids stable; lookup_method takes the first). Intentional per the comment, noted only for awareness.

Message-shape inconsistency between src/wasm/resolver.rs and src/native/resolver.rs for the same hermetic-resolution failure: the browser says 'alias '<name>' not declared in '<manifest>'' while the CLI says 'no packages.json above '<dir>' declares '<name>''. Worth unifying.
